text:
Happy Saturday! It's a frosty, crisp start in the upper 20s, with maybe a few high clouds around sunrise, so give the windshield a minute. High pressure is parked right on top of us, which means sunshine all day and hardly a breath of wind. The afternoon climbs to near 56, a touch warmer than most of the week so far, then tonight stays clear and chilly, around 35. No rain anywhere close, and there's still a little color left on the trees, so it's a good day for a walk.

Sunday is even nicer: sunny and warmer, near 61, though the models run from the upper 50s to the low 60s and I'd lean toward the warm end. A light south breeze picks up in the afternoon as the high slides east. A cold front comes through Monday afternoon and evening and could squeeze out a stray shower, but the air ahead of it is so dry that I'd bet on staying dry. The real change is Tuesday, when highs struggle to the mid 40s. Enjoy the weekend: a jacket for the morning, and you can shed it by afternoon.

AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-10-24T06:12:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. Beautiful weekend on tap for the North Country.
  2. Cold front on Monday may bring a few showers but dry weather is largely expected through the upcoming week.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 212 AM EDT Saturday... No significant changes have been made with this forecast package.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: There may be a few high clouds present at sunrise but sunny skies will prevail both today and Sunday. A 1033 mb high pressure has become well established across the region this morning and will remain in place through much of the day Sunday. As a result, winds will be light and variable throughout the day today. Winds will shift to the south at 7-12 mph Sunday afternoon as this high departs to the east and gradient flow begins to pick up. No precipitation is expected this weekend as high temperatures will be near or slightly above seasonal normals. KEY MESSAGE 2: A cold front is slated to move across the region during the second half of Monday. There are an increasing number of deterministic models and ensemble perturbations that are showing increasing rain chances Monday afternoon and evening across parts of the forecast area. However, the consensus is still favoring a mostly dry passage of the cold front. We have introduced some 20-30 PoPs for portions of northern New York and northern Vermont as a result but the antecedent dry air will likely make it very difficult for any rain to make it to the surface. Thereafter, temperatures on Tuesday will be noticeably cooler as highs will struggle to warm into the mid 40s. Another high pressure system, this one even stronger than the last, will move overhead on Wednesday which will allow the extended period of dry weather to continue. Temperatures will also moderate underneath this high pressure system with temps clicking back into the upper 40s to mid 50s on Wednesday. There is a chance we could see a frontal boundary approach from the west late next week but looks rather unimpressive at this time.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - The continued dry but pleasant weather will continue over the weekend. Today is starting off in the 20s for many locations along with partly cloudy skies, but the afternoon will become sunny and warmer with highs in the 50s. A few spots could hit 60 degrees. Sunday will continue the sunny skies with pleasant highs in the mid-50s to low 60s. The fall foliage is now past peak throughout the region, but some trees still have color, so the weekend will be great for viewing any remaining foliage. Overall, the week will remain dry, but the fire danger will remain relatively low due to a lack of wind. A cold front will come through on Monday. An isolated shower is possible, but most of the region is expected to remain dry. Highs will be in the 50s to around 60 degrees. The front will, however, usher in colder air for Tuesday. Despite mostly sunny skies, it will be chilly with highs in the 40s. Lows will be in the 20s, though some teens are expected. Wednesday and Thursday will be mostly sunny. Highs will be near 50 degrees on Wednesday, but Thursday’s highs will be closer to 60 degrees. Another system may bring a higher chance for showers on Friday, but no significant rain is in the forecast.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-10-23T15:51:00Z — same caveat): Sunshine through the weekend, turning warmer — Plan for one of the coldest nights of the season so far! Low temperatures bottom out in the teens and 20s early Saturday morning. This weekend will continue to have lots of sunshine. Highs reach the 50s Saturday, rebounding to the low and mid-60s for Sunday. Despite the enjoyable stretch, we'll have to watch for worsening drought and an increased brush fire risk due to the prolonged dry pattern.
